CPAC opposes unnecessary regulatory burdens that raise prices on American consumers and supported this resolution. data.billName: Stopping California’s Efforts to Gradually  Phase Out Gas-Powered Cars

textData.text: This resolution, sponsored by Rep. John James (CPAC Lifetime Rating 66%), invokes the Congressional Review Act to overturn an EPA waiver that had granted California authority to set vehicle emissions standards even stricter than federal law permits. The Congressional Review Act (CRA) is a law that lets Congress overturn federal agency regulations. After a federal agency creates a new rule, Congress has 60 legislative days to review it. If both houses of Congress pass a Joint Resolution of Disapproval and the President signs it, the rule is cancelled. California’s plan is to gradually burden gas cars with more and more regulations until gas cars become uneconomical. Since California is a large state, many auto manufacturers design their cars around California’s regulations, thus impacting the whole country. CPAC opposes California’s radical overregulation of vehicles that threatens consumer choice and drives up costs for all Americans, and supported this resolution.  The House passed the resolution on April 30, 2025, in a 231-191 vote (1 Republican voted against, and 13 Democrats voted in favor), and it later became law.
Republican Nay Vote: Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA)

data.billName: Stopping California’s Low Emissions Policy

textData.text: This resolution invokes the Congressional Review Act to take away California’s special exemption that allows them to implement a low NOx rule. The Congressional Review Act (CRA) is a law that lets Congress overturn federal agency regulations. After a federal agency creates a new rule, Congress has 60 legislative days to review it. If both houses of Congress pass a Joint Resolution of Disapproval and the President signs it, the rule is cancelled. CPAC opposes special regulatory carve-outs that allow California to impose its radical environmental agenda on consumers and supported this resolution. The Senate passed the motion on May 22, 2025, by a vote of 49-46 (all Republicans present voted in favor, and all Democrats present voted against), and President Donald J. Trump signed the measure into law on June 12, 2025.

data.billName: Stopping DoE Regulations on Commercial Refrigerator-Freezers

textData.text: This resolution invokes the Congressional Review Act to reject a Department of Energy rule that increases the price of already expensive commercial refrigerator-freezers. The Congressional Review Act (CRA) is a law that lets Congress overturn federal agency regulations. After a federal agency creates a new rule, Congress has 60 legislative days to review it. If both houses of Congress pass a Joint Resolution of Disapproval and the President signs it, the rule is cancelled.  CPAC opposes unnecessary regulatory burdens that raise prices for American consumers and supported this resolution. The resolution passed the Senate on May 1, 2025, by a vote of 52-45 (all Republicans present voted in favor, and all Democrats present voted against), and President Donald J. Trump signed the measure into law on May 9, 2025.

data.billName: Stopping Non-Citizens from Voting in DC Elections

August Pfluger (CPAC Lifetime Rating 83%), prohibits non-citizens from voting in District of Columbia elections and repeals the DC voting rights amendment of 2022. CPAC believes that voting is a sacred right of American citizens and opposes all non-citizens voting in American elections. For these reasons, CPAC supported this bill. The House passed the bill on June 10, 2025, by a vote of 266-148 (All Republicans and 56 Democrats voted in favor). The Senate has not taken floor action on the measure.

This amendment is similar to the Reins Act. CPAC supports reining in the unelected bureaucracy and strengthening congressional oversight, and supported this amendment. The Senate passed the amendment on February 21, 2025, by a vote of 53-47 (all Republicans voted in favor, and all Democrats voted against).

data.billName: Throwing Out an EPA Rule That Puts Excessive Restrictions on Natural Gas

If both houses of Congress pass a Joint Resolution of Disapproval and the President signs it, the rule is cancelled. CPAC opposes unnecessary regulatory burdens that inevitably raise energy prices for hardworking Americans and supported this resolution. Wade.  CPAC views abortion as a human tragedy, supports restrictions on the practice, and opposed this bill. The Senate voted against proceeding to the bill on July 10, 2024 by a vote of 49-44 (60 votes were needed to overcome the filibuster).

data.billName: Small Business Lending Under the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (Regulation B)

That Biden-supported DEI rule is enforced by the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau. CPAC opposes DEI and supported this effort to override Biden’s veto of the Congressional Review Act resolution. The Senate sustained the veto on January 10, 2024 by a vote of 54-45 (a 2/3 vote was needed).
